pr_title: Add quote handling in Verb, StrictModeVersion, Scope & PropertyType Argument Completers with single helper method
pr_body:
<!-- Anything that looks like this is a comment and can't be seen after the Pull Request is created. -->

# PR Summary

<!-- Summarize your PR between here and the checklist. -->

The below argument completers don't have support for quotes:

- `VerbArgumentCompleter`
- `StrictModeVersionArgumentCompleter`
- `ScopeArgumentCompleter`

This PR creates a static method `GetMatchingResults` which wraps the quote handling using `CompletionCompleters.HandleDoubleAndSingleQuote` and reuses this method across all these argument completers so quotes are handled in the same way. Happy to change this method name, I could not figure out a nicer name :D.

I also refactored `VerbArgumentCompleter` for `Get-Verb`/`Get-Command` to separate the actual cmdlet filtering and the completion methods, so it can also use this shared method like the other completers. Previously the cmdlet filtering and completion code were quite coupled but it makes more sense to separate these two since they both have different requirements, and it simplifies the code.

There are also more tests added to ensure single/double quotes are being handled correctly.

I've also ensured the `PropertyTypeArgumentCompleter` is using the same method which was already handling quotes in https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/pull/21117. 

## PR Context

Fixes PowerShell/PowerShell#24838

issue_context.title: Verb, StrictModeVersion and Scope Argument completers don't handle single/double quotes for parameter text completion
issue_context.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] Write a descriptive title.
- [x] Make sure you are able to repro it on the [latest released version](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/releases)
- [x] Search the existing issues.
- [x] Refer to the [FAQ](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/blob/master/docs/FAQ.md).
- [x] Refer to [Differences between Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/scripting/whats-new/differences-from-windows-powershell).

### Steps to reproduce

Currently for the following Argument Completers:

- `VerbArgumentCompleter`
- `StrictModeVersionArgumentCompleter`
- `ScopeArgumentCompleter`

There is no completion if the user inputs single quote `'` or double quote `"` before pressing TAB. This is because these argument completers do not use `HandleDoubleAndSingleQuote` in comparison to some other completers.

These completers should probably reuse a method which calls `HandleDoubleAndSingleQuote` so this logic can be shared across them.

### Expected behavior

```console
PS> Set-StrictMode -Version Lat -> Should complete to Latest
PS> Set-StrictMode -Version 'Lat -> Should complete to 'Latest'
PS> Set-StrictMode -Version "Lat -> Should complete to "Latest"

PS> Get-Variable -Scope Glo -> Should complete to Global
PS> Get-Variable -Scope 'Glo -> Should complete to 'Global'
PS> Get-Variable -Scope "Glo -> Should complete to "Global"
```

### Actual behavior

```console
PS> Set-StrictMode -Version Lat -> This completes to Latest
PS> Set-StrictMode -Version 'Lat -> This does not complete to 'Latest'
PS> Set-StrictMode -Version "Lat -> This does not complete to "Latest"

PS> Get-Variable -Scope Glo -> This completes to Global
PS> Get-Variable -Scope 'Glo -> This does not complete to 'Global'
PS> Get-Variable -Scope "Glo -> This does not complete to "Global"
```

review_comments: Since this is a general purpose function you should probably add some logic to escape special characters in the value.
@MartinGC94 Good catch. If there is no existing utility method which does this already I'll add that logic in.

Wonder if i can just use `Regex.Escape` or `WildcardPattern.Escape` here. Given we are just removing special characters for wildcard matching. Although I don't see much usage in existing code so wondering if I am missing something here?
I also think it would be worth parametrizing it with `bool escape` so it can be turned off incase for some reason we need to keep preserved string without escaping.

If the special characters are single and double quotas what are examples we could use for tests? 
I see here some escaping methods we could consider so I suggest to postpone this to keep the PR small.

It makes sense to delay this. I only find this useful if the input strings are not guaranteed to have special chars but currently none of the completers changed here have strings with special chars so perhaps we revisit when we refactor a completer that has special chars? It's probably also easier to review that in a separate PR.

I don't see any reason to include an option to disable the escaping. The only reason you'd want that is if you plan on doing additional processing and then escape them properly, but the method is generating complete completion results that cannot be modified anyway so that's hardly a concern.
As for how to implement it, you can take a look at the various suggestions in this thread: https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/issues/24493
@MartinGC94 Can you have a look at a297ab849d35f86952aa3c2592d488cb09843d6b. I have included code to do escaping on special chars, let me know if I'm missing anything.

There's a lot more problematic chars to handle, see this switch I use for escaping paths: https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/blob/master/src/System.Management.Automation/engine/CommandCompletion/CompletionCompleters.cs#L5003 some of them are unique to the path handling but many of them are not.  
To keep things simple I'd just use `IndexOfAny` to check for problematic characters: https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/blob/master/src/System.Management.Automation/engine/CommandCompletion/CompletionCompleters.cs#L5226 and if any are found, force single quotes and escape with: https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/blob/master/src/System.Management.Automation/engine/lang/codegen.cs#L21
@MartinGC94 Thanks. Let me know if a24641669c4580d2f6ae8b6778b0ee7a4dc06ad6 looks right. I will add some tests later if I get some time.
